/-!
# Erdős Problem 274

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/274](https://www.erdosproblems.com/274)
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzog%E2%80%93Sch%C3%B6nheim_conjecture)

@[expose] public section

open scoped Pointwise Cardinal

namespace Erdos274

-- TODO(callesonne): add already proved results from the wiki page

/-- An exact covering of a group `G` is a finite collection of subgroups `{H_1, ..., H_k}` and
representative `{g_1, ..., g_k}` such that the cosets `g_iH_i` are pairwise disjoint and their
union covers `G`.

Note that this differs from `Partition (α := Subgroup G)` because the covering condition there
invokes `Subgroup.sup` which is subgroup generation and thus stronger than union. This definition
is easier to use in this context than the alternative `Partition (α := Set G)`, which lacks
subgroup definitions such as `Subgroup.index`. -/
structure Group.ExactCovering (G : Type*) [Group G] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] where
  parts : ι → Subgroup G
  reps : ι → G
  nonempty (i : ι) : (parts i : Set G).Nonempty
  disjoint : (Set.univ (α := ι)).PairwiseDisjoint fun (i : ι) ↦ reps i • (parts i : Set G)
  covers : ⋃ i, reps i • (parts i : Set G) = Set.univ

/--
If $G$ is a group, can there exist an exact covering of $G$ by more than one coset
of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one of the cosets.)

The conjectured answer is no: in every such exact covering, two of the subgroups have
the same cardinality.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem erdos_274 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (G : Type*) (_ : Group G),
    1 < ENat.card G ∧ ∃ (ι : Type*) (_ : Fintype ι) (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι),
    1 < Fintype.card ι ∧ ∀ i j, i ≠ j → #(P.parts i) ≠ #(P.parts j) := by
  sorry

/--
If `G` is a finite abelian group then there cannot exist an exact covering of `G` by more
than one cosets of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one
of the cosets.)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 20,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Jostamon/erdos274-hs-abelian/blob/2ab8a2e39e7dd7836adf577b52555f069244466f/Erdos274/Main.lean"]
theorem erdos_274.variants.abelian {G : Type*} [Fintype G] [CommGroup G]
    (hG : 1 < Fintype.card G) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι)
    (hι : 1 < Fintype.card ι) :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ #(P.parts i) = #(P.parts j) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $G$ be a group, and let $A = \{a_1G_1, \dots, a_kG_k\}$ be a finite system of left cosets of
subgroups $G_1, \dots, G_k$ of $G$.

Herzog and Schönheim conjectured that if $A$ forms a partition of $G$ with $k > 1$, then the
indices $[G:G_1], \dots, [G:G_k]$ cannot be distinct.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem herzog_schonheim {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : 1 < ENat.card G) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (hι : 1 < Fintype.card ι) (P : Group.ExactCovering G ι) :
    ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ (P.parts i).index = (P.parts j).index := by
  sorry

end Erdos274

reformulations.difference: Unlike the explicit finite-index formulation in Margolis–Schnabel, the Lean statement does not assume that the subgroups have finite index. It uses the natural-number-valued Subgroup.index and adds 1 < ENat.card G.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Neumann's covering theorem allows infinite-index cosets to be removed from any finite coset cover. In an ExactCovering every coset is nonempty and disjoint from the others, so none can be removed: every part therefore has finite index. Consequently, Subgroup.index's infinite-index default of 0 is unreachable. Moreover, more than one disjoint nonempty coset forces G to be nontrivial, making the extra cardinality hypothesis redundant. These facts and the resulting statement equivalence are proved as Review274.finiteIndex_parts, group_nontrivial, and hsc_source_form_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The finite abelian variant concludes that two subgroup cardinalities coincide, whereas the cited Herzog–Schönheim results conclude that two subgroup indices coincide.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For subgroups H and K of a finite group G, Lagrange's theorem gives |H|[G:H] = |G| = |K|[G:K], with all factors positive. Thus |H| = |K| if and only if [G:H] = [G:K]. Left multiplication also identifies each subgroup bijectively with its coset. The cardinality/index equivalence and its existential repeated-value form are proved as Review274.finite_card_eq_iff_index_eq and repeated_card_iff_index in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: All declarations were checked; no mathematical or status defects were found. The main answer slot has the source's existence polarity. Scratch proofs verify that ExactCovering is equivalent to unique coset membership, handle empty and singleton indexing, construct a nontrivial two-element example, and show that distinct subgroup sizes force G to be finite (all parts of an infinite-group exact covering have cardinality |G|). The cited abelian proof and its dependencies were compiled in the sandbox. A namespace-renamed copy plus a field-for-field bridge proves this file's exact abelian statement; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The general OPEN and abelian solved records agree with the sources.
